label: diplostemonous
definition: A structural quality inhering in an androecium by virtue of its consisting of two whorls of stamens, the outer whorl opposite the sepals and the inner whorl opposite the petals. NOTE: Botany-specific; follows FLOPO:0991167 didynamous. Statements on 'stamens' or 'flower' are moved to the androecium.
reason: A standard androecium character with no PATO or FLOPO term; it is more than a stamen count, because it fixes how the two whorls sit against the perianth.
'Diversement colorées' says that the colour varies between plants or forms, not that one organ has a colour pattern; mapping it to PATO_0001533 multi-colored would overstate it.
A cut-off fragment of 'foliaceous', which rule C187 already maps to leaf-like (PATO_0002457). A rule on 'foli' would also catch foliolate and similar words.
A fusion to another part ('adnate to'), which the relation pattern holds as the quality plus the other part, not as a term of its own.
'Staminal tube garni d'anthères' says the tube bears anthers: anther present on the staminal tube (FLOPO_0986013).
French 'grumeleux' describes a finely lumpy, knobbly surface of seeds and exocarp, which is closest to tuberculate. PATO_0001759 granular is about what a thing contains, not its surface.

label: hypogeal
definition: A positional quality inhering in a seedling by virtue of its cotyledons remaining below the soil surface, usually within the seed coat, during germination. NOTE: Botany-specific; an epigeal sibling (cotyledons raised above the soil) is expected. Not FLOPO:0991035 subterranean, which is about where an organ grows, not about germination.
reason: Hypogeal germination is a standard seedling character with no PATO or FLOPO term.

label: incumbent
definition: A positional quality inhering in the cotyledons of an embryo by virtue of the radicle being folded so that it lies against the back of one cotyledon. NOTE: Botany-specific (Brassicaceae); sibling of accumbent, where the radicle lies against the edges of the cotyledons.
reason: A standard character of how the embryo is folded; PATO has no term for it.

label: induplicate-valvate
definition: A valvate quality inhering in a perianth by virtue of the margins of its adjacent members being folded inward where they meet without overlapping in bud. NOTE: Child of FLOPO:0991083 valvate.
reason: A named kind of valvate bud arrangement, not two values run together; it sits under the existing FLOPO valvate.
Margins rolled inward are involute: PATO_0001962, 'edges rolled inwards spirally on each side'.
It names a direction of growth, with no shape or size it is compared to; without the context it means nothing.
Laticiferous plants and bark have latex-containing laticifer cells (PO_0025031, 'a ground tissue cell that contains latex').
A lax-flowered inflorescence has loosely set flowers; this is the same mapping as rule C169 lax → loose.
French 'lianeux' (liana-like) is the same as lianescent, which rule C354 maps to climbing.
The two statements name a lip-like part ('widened into a lip at the apex', 'stigmas forming lips'), not one defined shape. A two-lipped organ is already FLOPO:0991085 bilabiate.
'2-locular', '3- or 5-locular' are counts of locules; 'locular' is already in config/flora_counted_parts.tsv (→ locule).
French 'déhiscence loculicide' is loculicidal dehiscence.
A leaf 'bordered by a marginal vein', with the secondary veins joined into it, has the vein just inside the margin that PO calls intramarginal vein.
A count of ovules ('ovulate' → ovule in flora_counted_parts.tsv) with no number; like 'many', it is held as not numeric rather than given a term.
A count of seeds per fruit ('seeded' → seed) with no number; it is treated like 'many'.
Rule C194 maps canaliculate to PATO_0002255 grooved, so this is its negation.

label: paludicolous
definition: A positional quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its growing rooted in marshes or swamps, in waterlogged ground. NOTE: Probably outside PATO's scope (where an organism lives); kept in FLOPO beside FLOPO:0991111 terrestrial, FLOPO:0991112 aquatic and FLOPO:0991193 emergent.
